title: Align stakeholders and create fast-track rollback gates for PRD scope shifts
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Purpose: establish a lightweight, documented pathway for fast decisioning and rollback when PRD scope shifts are proposed during implementation for Structured Output v2. We aim to reduce approval latency while preserving legal and security guardrails and minimizing rework for eng/design. The ticket creates: 1) an owner matrix (decision owner, review owner, contingency owner) per change class; 2) scope-freeze windows and emergency fast-track lanes; 3) explicit acceptance lanes with measurable criteria (telemetry guards); and 4) a rollback playbook tied to deployment artifacts and dashboards.

Context & motivation: recent scope clarifications on prompt-eval and structured-output mappings caused a 2-week slip in runtime rollout and added rework for infra and design. Teams have requested a predictable sign-off path that balances speed and auditability. We must account for: legal/data residency checks, design contract stability, runtime performance regressions, and telemetry gaps.

Scope: this ticket covers the governance and operational artifacts (matrix, runbook, decision SLA, telemetry guard thresholds). It does NOT change the PRD feature scope itself or implement guardrails in code — those are follow-up action items assigned to ENG/DES/LEGAL owners.

Trade-offs considered: - Narrower fast-track (product + eng only) reduces latency but increases legal/regulatory risk; we keep legal in the loop for any change impacting data handling or user-facing text. - Strict scope freezes reduce churn but can delay urgent bug fixes; we separate 'bug/security' lane from 'feature-scope' lane with different SLAs. - Automated telemetry gates vs manual signoff: pursue telemetry-first with manual override for exceptions; require documented rationale for overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Owner matrix published: for each change class (minor wording, UI contract, runtime perf, data-handling) assign Decision Owner, Review Owner, and Contingency Owner with contact details.
Scope-freeze windows and the fast-track flow documented in Confluence with step-by-step responsibilities and expected SLA (max 48 hours for fast-track review, 72 hours for full review).
Telemetry gate definitions added for runtime regressions: CPU p95 increase > 15% OR tail latency (99th) > 40ms triggers automatic rollback lane and on-call paging to infra.
Legal checklist included for any change that touches PII, data routing, or external integrations; legal signoff is required for changes flagged by the checklist.
Rollback playbook created with exact rollback artifacts (model-version pin, route switch command, dashboard links) and a tested dry-run scenario documented.
All cross-team reviewers (ENG, DESIGN, LEGAL, SECURITY) acknowledged the runbook and owner matrix in a comment on the Confluence page.
At least one simulated fast-track approval and rollback exercise completed and notes added to the playbook (runbook exercise date and participants).
